title: 3D Printing Rock Art Panel
author: Nur Ihsan
materials: File Format: Configure the camera to capture images in JPEG format at the highest resolution available. For best results withhighest resolution and wider color range, shoot with RAW format (NEF, CR2, PEF, etc.), as most of the photogrammetry tutorial suggested. This setting will also beneficial if you want to reliably document the rock art panel for the purpose of general preservation. However, it will require us to do a preprocessing step such as convert the RAW files to JPEG in the next section. Also, the color accuracy is not necessarily needed since the painting will be presented not in digital format and the color reproduction will rely on the paint mixture by the artist. Furthermore, the level of detail that we get from this processing will most likely get destroyed in the subsequent steps in the 3D modelling section.
Duplicate the chunk and assign an appropriate name.

steps.title: Place coded markers
steps.instruction: Position the Ground Control Point (GCP) markers evenly around the outer rim of the rock‑art panel using a non‑residue adhesive; do not place markers on or near the paintings.

steps.title: Setup total station
steps.instruction: Establish the total station using the site’s geodetic datum, or if unavailable, the local coordinate system; perform required calibration.

steps.title: Configure LED lighting
steps.instruction: If natural light is insufficient, arrange several LED lights to illuminate the panel evenly and adjust intensity to avoid casting shadows.

steps.title: Record marker coordinates
steps.instruction: Measure each GCP with the total station and store the coordinate as “target n”, where n is the marker number.

steps.title: Capture inner panel points
steps.instruction: Record coordinates at clear‑edge points inside the panel, photograph each point while the total‑station laser is active for later photogrammetry alignment.

steps.title: Set camera parameters
steps.instruction: Fix zoom‑lens focal length to its shortest setting; use Manual mode (or Aperture mode with minimum 1/80 s shutter). Set aperture between f/5.6–f/16 (f/8 typical). Set ISO 640 and shutter speed 1/80 s. Plan the shooting direction based on panel and cave floor topography.

steps.title: Photograph panel – vertical pass
steps.instruction: From the starting point, take vertical images from top to bottom with 75‑85 % vertical overlap.

steps.title: Photograph panel – reverse pass
steps.instruction: Move one step along the planned direction, then photograph from bottom to top with 85‑90 % side overlap; repeat until the whole surface is covered and then retrieve all markers.

steps.title: Transfer images to computer
steps.instruction: Copy all photos from the memory card to a new folder on the same drive as the operating system (SSD) to avoid SSD/HDD transfer bottlenecks.

steps.title: Import images into Metashape
steps.instruction: Launch Agisoft Metashape, add all photos as a single chunk via Workflow > Add Photos.

steps.title: Save Metashape project
steps.instruction: Save the project in the root directory of the image folder with an appropriate file name.

steps.title: Estimate image quality
steps.instruction: Right‑click a photo, choose Estimate Image Quality → All Cameras; after processing, disable any image with quality < 0.5.

steps.title: Align photos
steps.instruction: Select Workflow > Align Photos and use the alignment parameters shown in the reference image.

steps.title: Add marker reference
steps.instruction: In the Reference pane, open Settings, set the coordinate system, and check the ‘Marker reference’ box.

steps.title: Detect coded markers
steps.instruction: Tools > Markers > Detect Markers…, choose ‘Circular 12 bit’, leave all other parameters at default.

steps.title: Import CSV coordinates
steps.instruction: Click Import reference, set the coordinate system, delimiter, and column structure, then load the CSV file with marker coordinates.

steps.title: Place non‑marker points
steps.instruction: Find photos containing each non‑marker reference (see Step 5), right‑click the point, select Place Marker, assign the correct point name, and repeat for all such points.

steps.title: Update transform
steps.instruction: In the Reference pane, click the ‘Update Transform’ button.

steps.title: Duplicate chunk for rollback
steps.instruction: Right‑click the current chunk, choose Duplicate, rename the copy by appending ‘pre‑optimization’ to serve as a rollback point.

steps.title: Optimize camera alignment
steps.instruction: Tools > Optimize Cameras; keep default parameters (f, k1‑k3, cx, cy, p1, p2) and enable ‘Estimate tie point covariance’ and ‘Fit additional corrections’.

steps.title: Remove weak tie points – reconstruction uncertainty
steps.instruction: Open Gradual Selection → Reconstruction Uncertainty, set Level = 10 (reduce by 1 if > 50 % of tie points are selected), delete selected points, then repeat Step 15 (optimize cameras).

steps.title: Remove weak tie points – projection accuracy
steps.instruction: Open Gradual Selection → Projection Accuracy, set Level = 3 (decrease by 0.1 until ≤ 50 % of points are selected), delete selected points, then repeat Step 15.

steps.title: Remove weak tie points – reprojection error
steps.instruction: Open Gradual Selection → Reprojection Error, set Level = 0.3 (or adjust to keep ≈ 10 % of points), delete selected points, then repeat Step 15 with all camera parameters and ‘Fit additional corrections’ checked.

steps.title: Build dense cloud
steps.instruction: Workflow > Build Dense Cloud; set Quality = High, Depth Filtering = Moderate, and enable ‘Calculate point colors’ and ‘Calculate point confidence’.

steps.title: Activate new chunk
steps.instruction: Double‑click the new chunk name in the Workspace pane so it appears in bold.

steps.title: Clean dense point cloud
steps.instruction: Use the free‑form selection tool to delete unnecessary points and refine the panel edge by zooming in and removing stray points until the desired shape is achieved.

steps.title: Build mesh
steps.instruction: Workflow > Build Mesh to generate an open‑geometry mesh.

steps.title: Build textured model
steps.instruction: Workflow > Build Textured Model.

steps.title: Export model files
steps.instruction: File > Export Model; save both .obj (with texture) and .stl (open geometry) using appropriate names.

steps.title: Import STL into Meshmixer
steps.instruction: Launch Meshmixer 3.5 on Windows 11 and open the exported STL file.

steps.title: Set model units to meters
steps.instruction: Actions > Units → set one dimension to meters, keep X/Y/Z values unchanged, click Done.

steps.title: Orient model correctly
steps.instruction: Edit > Transform; set View Cube to Front, rotate/move the model until its front aligns with the view, then Accept.

steps.title: Select model boundary
steps.instruction: Select tool → zoom in, double‑click the blue line around the model to select all connected triangle meshes at the boundary.

steps.title: Expand and optimize boundary
steps.instruction: Modify > Optimize Boundary → Expand Ring 2–3 times (≈ 10 cm) to push the boundary inward; repeat Optimize Boundary as needed.

steps.title: Smooth boundary
steps.instruction: Select > Modify > Smooth Boundary; adjust parameters until the edge is smooth, then Accept.

steps.title: Optional smooth with deform
steps.instruction: With the boundary still selected, choose Deform > Smooth and tweak parameters until the boundary is nearly flat.

steps.title: Extrude model surface
steps.instruction: Select the front side of the model, Modify > Select All, then Edit > Extrude; set extrusion height (e.g., 20 cm for 1:2 scale or 10 cm for full size) and adjust other parameters to avoid non‑manifold geometry.

steps.title: Export edited STL
steps.instruction: Export the modified model as an .stl file with a distinctive name for later processing.

steps.title: Import STL into Fusion 360
steps.instruction: Open Fusion 360, go to File > Open, and load the exported STL file.

steps.title: Adjust orientation if needed
steps.instruction: If required, use Modify > Move/Copy to rotate and position the model for optimal splitting.

steps.title: Partition model into sections
steps.instruction: Create an offset plane (Construct > Offset Plane) on a face, set the offset distance for the first 20 × 20 cm split, then Modify > Split Body using that plane; repeat with new offset planes until the entire model is divided into 20 cm squares.

steps.title: Create half‑cylinder pegs
steps.instruction: Create > Cylinder on a split face, set desired diameter and height; then Modify > Split Body with a bisecting plane, delete one half, and repeat for every joint where a peg is needed.

steps.title: Insert pegs and cut holes
steps.instruction: Insert > Insert Mesh to place a peg STL into a joint, use Modify > Move/Copy for positioning; then Modify > Combine, set Target Body = part, Tool Body = peg, Operation = Cut, keep tools checked; repeat for the opposite part and for all joints.

steps.title: Export modified parts
steps.instruction: Select each part individually, File > Export, choose STL, and assign a unique name; repeat for all parts.

steps.title: Import parts into PrusaSlicer
steps.instruction: Open PrusaSlicer, use File > Open to load all STL part files.

steps.title: Set slicing parameters for parts
steps.instruction: Filament = PLA; Nozzle diameter = 0.6 mm; Infill = Lightning at 20 %; Layer height = 0.4 mm; enable Generate Support Material and adjust overhang threshold and first‑layer support as needed.

steps.title: Position parts on print bed
steps.instruction: Select each part and use the ‘Place on Face’ tool so that the joint stands upright on the bed.

steps.title: Slice parts and generate G‑code
steps.instruction: Click ‘Slice Now’ to create G‑code for each part.

steps.title: Scale and slice pegs
steps.instruction: Import the peg STL, scale to 98 % (Object manipulation > Scale), keep the same slicing parameters but change Infill to Gyroid at 20 % and Perimeters to 2; then Slice Now.

steps.title: Export all G‑code files
steps.instruction: For each sliced part and peg, use File > Export G‑code, assigning distinctive filenames; repeat for all files.

steps.title: Start 3D printing
steps.instruction: Copy the G‑code files to the printer’s thumb drive and start each print on the 3D printer.

steps.title: Assemble printed parts
steps.instruction: Insert each peg into its corresponding hole; tap gently with a rubber mallet if needed to achieve a snug fit.

steps.title: Apply resin epoxy glue
steps.instruction: Apply a thin layer of resin epoxy glue to pegs and inside of holes, join the parts, hold pressure until the glue sets; repeat for all joints.

steps.title: Smooth joints after curing
steps.instruction: Once the glue has fully cured, sand the joints starting with coarse‑grit sandpaper and progressing to finer grits for a smooth finish.

steps.title: Prime the assembled model
steps.instruction: Apply a uniform coat of primer paint over the entire model to improve paint adhesion.

steps.title: Replicate rock‑art painting
steps.instruction: Using appropriate paints and techniques, the artist reproduces the original rock‑art on the primed model, allowing adequate drying time between coats and following all material manufacturer instructions.
